edges.description: Na+-dependent excitatory amino acid and GABA transporters lose the Na+ gradient they use for reuptake.

edges.description: Persisting synaptic transmitter drives neuronal hyperactivity, marked by c-Fos induction, which is followed by selective apoptosis in the regions of highest alpha-2 density.

edges.description: Joint contractures from joints that were never moved.

Hydrops accompanies the sequence. The route from akinesia to fluid accumulation is not established in this disorder, so the intermediates are unknown.
The compressed dysmorphic facies of a fetus that did not move.
Respiratory insufficiency is the stated cause of neonatal death in this disorder.
Raised intracellular chloride was measured directly in ventrolateral medullary neurons of the null mouse, and the alpha-2/KCC2 interaction was shown by co-immunoprecipitation.
Respiratory motoneuron output is defective before birth and the mouse dies of lack of breathing, matching the human cause of death.
The mouse shows c-Fos induction followed by selective neuronal apoptosis, but in the amygdala and piriform cortex rather than in the basal ganglia where the human injury is seen.
edges.limitations: The region affected differs from the human pattern, so the model supports the mechanism without reproducing its anatomical distribution.
